capability_investigated:
The feature-extraction + batched-decode path: processor() always pads/
truncates audio to one 30s (3000-frame) mel window, and generate() accepts a
batched feature view (N,80,3000) paired with one prompt per item.
what_i_learned:
The stub's single processor() call hard-caps coverage at the first 30s, so on
multi-minute 0715 calls almost the entire reference is deleted (length_ratio
floored). generate() decodes N stacked windows in a single call, so full-file
coverage costs one batched decode per file rather than N sequential calls.
hypothesis:
Slice audio into consecutive 30s windows, stack their mel features, decode the
whole batch at once, and join the per-window text. This directly attacks the
dominant deletion axis by transcribing the tail the stub threw away, while the
batched call keeps runtime inside the budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension vs GPU memory: how peak CUDA allocation scales
with the number of stacked (80,3000) mel windows passed in one decode call.
what_i_learned:
generate() does NOT stream the batch — passing all N windows of a multi-minute
file as one (N,80,3000) view makes the whole batch resident on the GPU at once
and OOMs. The batch dimension is bounded by VRAM, not just by API acceptance;
one-window-per-call keeps peak memory flat at single-window size.
hypothesis:
Keep the full-file 30s windowing that fixes the deletion/length_ratio floor,
but decode each window in its own generate() call instead of one batched call,
so coverage no longer trades against an OOM crash.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_size decoding kwarg on the per-window decode path — how the
CT2 Whisper search width changes within-window coverage versus the greedy
(beam_size=1) decode the parent uses.
what_i_learned:
The parent already covers the full audio (every 30s window is decoded), yet
length_ratio is only 0.65 and repeated_text fires on 4/12 files. So the
deletion is intra-window, not coverage-of-audio: greedy beam=1 decode collapses
into repetition loops / early EOS inside a window and strands the rest of that
window's speech. CT2 generate() does NOT auto-fallback on temperature, so beam
width is the available robustness lever against greedy collapse.
hypothesis:
Raise beam_size 1->5 on the per-window decode. Wider beam search avoids the
greedy looping/early-termination that deletes the tail of each window, lifting
length_ratio and cutting repeated_text against the dominant deletion axis;
~5x of 103.8s inference still fits the 719.9s budget.
